Enum Class ScreenRegion

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<ScreenRegion>
com.trevlar.menukit.core.ScreenRegion
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<ScreenRegion>, Constable
public enum ScreenRegion extends Enum<ScreenRegion>
A spot on the SCREEN edge — the nine-spot screen-edge vocabulary: the four corners, the four edge midpoints, and the centre. This is the ONE screen-edge region type in MenuKit; it backs two distinct placement subsystems that share this single vocabulary:
  • Single-panel chrome (RegionMath.resolveScreenRegion(ScreenRegion, int, int, int, int, int)) — pins ONE Panel to a fixed screen spot, inset by a caller-supplied margin, independent of the screen's content. Used by PanelPosition.screenAnchor(ScreenRegion) so chrome like a "< Back" button (TOP_LEFT) or a screen title (TOP_CENTER) stays put regardless of how the content sizes, wraps, or scrolls. This placement never fails (a too-big panel just overhangs the far edge) and does not stack. Screen-anchored panels are excluded from the layout's extent, exactly as overlay (centred) panels are.
  • Vanilla-screen injection stacking (RegionMath.resolveVanillaScreen(ScreenRegion, int, int, int, int, int), via VanillaScreenPanelAdapter) — STACKS multiple injected panels against the bounds of a vanilla non-container Screen (Options, Controls/KeyBinds, world-select, server-list). Anchors to the screen's GUI-scaled width × height (no inventory chrome — vanilla non-container screens have none), inset by RegionConstants.EDGE_INSET, with same- region panels stacking VERTICALLY at RegionConstants.SCREEN_STACK_GAP (down from top edges, up from bottom edges, down from vertical-center). This placement returns OUT_OF_REGION when a panel overflows, and orders siblings by the RegionAnchor priority below.

Where PanelPosition.region(MenuRegion) anchors a panel to the MAIN panel's bounds (so it moves with the content frame), screenAnchor pins to a fixed SCREEN spot. The two resolvers above are deliberately distinct geometries over the same nine names — the chrome path is single-shot, the injection path is prefix-stacked — which is why a single enum serves both.

This unified ScreenRegion replaces the former pair of identical nine-spot enums (ScreenRegion for chrome + VanillaScreenRegion for injection): they were the same alphabet backing two subsystems, so they collapse into this one type, which carries the richer priority(int) surface the injection path needs while the chrome path simply ignores it.

Layout constants live in RegionConstants (the per-enum STACK_GAP/EDGE_INSET faces were hoisted there so all four region enums present an identical surface): read RegionConstants.SCREEN_STACK_GAP / RegionConstants.EDGE_INSET / RegionConstants.SCREEN_EDGE_MARGIN directly.

    • priority

      public RegionAnchor<ScreenRegion> priority(int priority)
      Returns a RegionAnchor pairing this region with an explicit stacking priority. Lower priority renders first (closer to the region's anchor edge); default is RegionAnchor.DEFAULT_PRIORITY.

      Consumed only by the vanilla-screen INJECTION path (which stacks several panels in one region); the single-panel chrome path (screenAnchor/resolveScreenRegion) ignores priority. Mirrors HudRegion.priority(int) / MenuRegion.priority(int), so all stacking-family region enums present an identical surface.
